definition: The act of combining, the state of being combined or the result of combining.

Combine A and B (together) Combine the eggs and the flour.

definition: A choric song of celebration or revel, especially in Ancient Greece.

definition: Providing physical comfort and ease; agreeable.

definition: Funny; amusing; comical.

definition: A comedian.

definition: A person who comments; especially someone who is paid to give his/her opinions in the media about current affairs, sports, etc.

He's one of the great sports commentators of our time.

definition: The exchange or buying and selling of commodities; especially the exchange of merchandise, on a large scale, between different places or communities; extended trade or traffic.

definition: Of or pertaining to commerce.
examples: A commercial vehicle (= one that is used for carrying goods or passengers who pay)
Commercial activities

definition: An advertisement in a common media format, usually radio or television.

definition: A sending or mission (to do or accomplish something).

definition: To send or officially charge someone or some group to do something.

definition: A member of a commission.

The Church Commissioners (= the group of people responsible for controlling the financial affairs of the Church of England)

definition: To give in trust; to put into charge or keeping; to entrust; to consign; used with to or formerly unto.

To commit an act of violence/terrorism

definition: The act or an instance of committing, putting in charge, keeping, or trust, especially:.

He has served on numerous committees.

definition: Anything movable (a good) that is bought and sold.
examples: Crude oil is the world's most important commodity.
A drop in commodity prices

Allergies to milk are quite common in childhood.

definition: As a rule; frequently; usually.

These fats are commonly found in processed foods.

definition: To impart.

Communicate with somebody/something Dolphins use sound to communicate with each other.

definition: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.

Non-verbal communication such as gestures or facial expressions

definition: A group sharing a common understanding, and often the same language, law, manners, and/or tradition.
examples: It is hoped that the campaign will encourage members of the community to get active.
In/within the community health workers based in the community (= working with people in a local area)

definition: A friend, acquaintance, or partner; someone with whom one spends time or keeps company.
examples: Geoff was my companion on the journey.
(figurative) Fear was the hostages' constant companion.

definition: A team; a group of people who work together professionally.
examples: Company profits were 5 per cent lower than last year.
He works for the National Bus Company.

definition: (often with to) Able to be compared (to).
examples: Inflation is now at a rate comparable with that in other European countries.
Comparable in something The two machines are comparable in size.

definition: Of or relating to comparison.
examples: Then he was living in comparative comfort (= compared with others or with his own life at a previous time).
The company is a comparative newcomer to the software market (= other companies have been in business much longer).

examples: How can you compare the two things? They are so different!
We compared the two reports carefully.

definition: The act of comparing or the state or process of being compared.
examples: The two situations bear no comparison (= they are not at all similar).

definition: Deep awareness of the suffering of another, coupled with the wish to relieve it.
examples: She was known as a hard woman with no compassion, no emotion.
To feel/show compassion

definition: To drive together, round up.

The court has powers to compel witnesses to attend.

definition: Strongly or irresistibly evoking interest or attention.
examples: Her latest book makes compelling reading.
His eyes were strangely compelling.

definition: To do (something good) after (something bad) happens.

definition: The act or principle of compensating.
examples: She received a cash sum by way of compensation.
In compensation to receive £10 000 in compensation

definition: To be in battle or in a rivalry with another for the same thing, position, or reward; to contend.

definition: The quality or state of being competent, i.e. able or suitable for a general role.

Professional/technical competence

definition: The action of competing.

The youngest competitor in the event

The flavours in the dish complement each other perfectly.

definition: To finish; to make done; to reach the end.

definition: (manner) In a complete manner.

The road is nearing completion (= it is nearly finished).

definition: Made up of multiple parts; composite; not simple.

A highly complex situation

definition: A network of interconnected systems.

A sports/leisure/shopping complex

definition: The state of being complex; intricacy; entanglement.

definition: An act of complying.

definition: Difficult or convoluted.

A complicated issue/process/system

definition: The act or process of complicating.

definition: To yield assent; to accord; to acquiesce, agree, consent; to adapt oneself, to conform.
examples: What sanctions can they take against us if we fail to comply?
When requested to leave, they refused to comply.

definition: A smaller, self-contained part of a larger entity. Often refers to a manufactured object that is part of a larger device.

Component in something Trust is a vital component in any relationship.

definition: To make something by merging parts.

definition: One who composes; an author.

definition: The act of putting together; assembly.

The size and composition of an average class

The air smelled like a compound of diesel and petrol fumes.

definition: Broadly or completely covering; including a large proportion of something.

Comprehensive insurance (= covering all risks)

definition: To be made up of; to consist of (especially a comprehensive list of parts).

A compromise solution/agreement/candidate

definition: Cautious.

definition: The act of consulting.

definition: Someone who contains; something that contains.

definition: Argument, contest, debate, strife, struggle.

definition: Controversy; debate.

definition: To contend.

The average annual salary for those jobs was $90 721.

definition: A hall.
examples: She gets 10 per cent commission on each sale.
I haven't made a sale all week.

definition: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
examples: A pinch of salt (= a small amount of it)
Sprinkle with salt to taste.

definition: Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; identical.
examples: Gary and I look more or less the same age.
I recognized a lot of the same people.

definition: Together.
examples: We treat boys exactly the same as girls.
(informal) He gave me five dollars, same as usual.

definition: A part or snippet of something taken or presented for inspection, or shown as evidence of the quality of the whole; a specimen.
examples: The survey covers a representative sample of schools.
We studied a large population sample.

definition: To take or to test a sample or samples of.
examples: He put his head out of the window and sampled the morning air.
We simply had to stop and sample some road-side cuisine.

definition: An approval, by an authority, generally one that makes something valid.
examples: Trade sanctions were imposed against any country that refused to sign the agreement.
The economic sanctions have been lifted.

definition: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
examples: His hair was the colour of sand.
The resort has its own white sand beach.

definition: A dish or foodstuff where two or more slices of bread serve as the wrapper or container of some other food.
examples: We ate turkey sandwiches and wild blueberries.
A grilled cheese sandwich

definition: A moon or other smaller body orbiting a larger one.
examples: They have successfully launched satellites into orbit.
The software enables the user to set up a satellite communications link.

definition: A fulfilment of a need or desire.
examples: To gain/get/derive satisfaction from something
She didn't want to give him the satisfaction of seeing her cry.

definition: In a state of satisfaction.
examples: The Olympic athlete was satisfied with her performance.
They were not satisfied with the outcome of the talks.

definition: To do enough for; to meet the needs of; to fulfill the wishes or requirements of.
examples: The proposed plan will not satisfy everyone.
Nothing satisfies him—he's always complaining.

definition: The day of the week after Friday and before Sunday.
examples: (informal or North American English) We'll meet Saturday.
I work Saturdays to Wednesdays.

definition: A liquid (often thickened) condiment or accompaniment to food.
examples: Coconut tart served with hot chocolate sauce
Tomato/cranberry/chilli sauce

definition: To prevent harm or difficulty.
examples: Save somebody/something from something to save a rare species from extinction
This new technology might just have the power to save the world from ecological disaster.

definition: A reduction in cost or expenditure.
examples: The new building enjoys energy savings of 25 percent annually.
The service has delivered significant cost savings.

definition: A chance to speak; the right or power to influence or make a decision.
examples: Say (in something) We had no say in the decision to sell the company.
People want a greater say in local government.

definition: To pronounce.
examples: + speech ‘Hello!’ she said.
A legendary football coach once said, ‘Winning is everything.’

definition: A ladder; a series of steps; a means of ascending.
examples: Manufacturing is done on a small scale.
On a … scale They entertain on a large scale (= they hold expensive parties with a lot of guests).

definition: To examine sequentially, carefully, or critically; to scrutinize; to behold closely.
examples: Scan for something You should teach students to scan for essential information.
Scan something for something I scanned the list quickly for my name.

definition: An incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the persons or organization involved.
examples: A promising career wrecked by scandal
To cause/create a scandal

definition: A minor fright.
examples: Scare tactics (= ways of persuading people to do something by frightening them)
A scare story (= a news report that spreads more anxiety or fear about something than is necessary)

definition: To frighten, terrify, startle, especially in a minor way.
examples: It scares somebody to do something It scared me to think I was alone in the building.
Scare somebody You scared me.

definition: Feeling fear; afraid, frightened.
examples: Scared at something He was scared at the prospect of running out of food.
Scared (that)… I’m scared (that) I’m going to fall.

definition: Causing or able to cause fright.
examples: Close up the statue looked even more scary.
It was a pretty scary experience.

definition: Seemingly randomly distributed.
examples: Her family are scattered around the world.
Sunshine with scattered showers

definition: An outline of the plot of a dramatic or literary work.
examples: The worst-case scenario (= the worst possible thing that could happen) would be for the factory to be closed down.
A nightmare scenario

definition: The location of an event that attracts attention.
examples: The scene of the accident/crime/crash
On the scene Firefighters arrived on the scene within minutes.

definition: Having, or expressing doubt; questioning.
examples: She looked highly sceptical.
Sceptical about something I am sceptical about his chances of winning.

definition: A slip of paper; a short note.
examples: The countries have yet to set the schedule for the next round of talks.
I have no time available in my regular schedule.

definition: To create a time-schedule.
examples: Schedule something We scheduled regular status meetings.
Local elections were tentatively scheduled for November.

definition: A systematic plan of future action.
examples: A salary/insurance/loan scheme
To introduce/launch/run a scheme

definition: A student; one who studies at school or college, typically having a scholarship.
examples: He was the most distinguished scholar in his field.

definition: A grant-in-aid to a student.
examples: On a scholarship He went to drama school on a scholarship.
She won a scholarship to study at Stanford.

definition: (collective) A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
examples: (formal) Which school do they attend?
A girls'/boys' school

definition: A particular discipline or branch of learning, especially one dealing with measurable or systematic principles rather than intuition or natural ability.
examples: The advance of modern science
New developments in science and technology

definition: Of, or having to do with science.
examples: A scientific discovery/theory/fact
Sites of scientific interest

definition: One whose activities make use of the scientific method to answer questions regarding the measurable universe. A scientist may be involved in original research, or make use of the results of the research of others.
examples: Scientists and engineers
Scientists believe there is ice a few inches below the surface of Mars.

definition: The breadth, depth or reach of a subject; a domain.
examples: Scope (for somebody) (to do something) The extra money will give us the scope to improve our facilities.
Within somebody's scope First try to do something that is within your scope.

definition: The total number of goals, points, runs, etc. earned by a participant in a game.
examples: I’ll keep (the) score.
What's the score now?

definition: To cut a notch or a groove in a surface.
examples: The only man to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final
Score something to score a goal/try/touchdown/victory/point/run

definition: A disruption, mark or shallow cut on a surface made by scratching.
examples: Without a scratch He escaped without a scratch (= was not hurt at all).
It's only a scratch (= a very slight injury).

definition: To rub a surface with a sharp object, especially by a living creature to remove itching with nails, claws, etc.
examples: Scratch (yourself) The dog scratched itself behind the ear.
Scratch something John yawned and scratched his chin.

definition: A loud, emphatic, exclamation of extreme emotion, especially horror, fear, excitement, or anger; it may comprise a word or a sustained, high-pitched vowel sound.
examples: He drove off with a scream of tyres.
They ignored the baby's screams.

definition: To cry out with a shrill voice; to utter a sudden, sharp outcry, or shrill, loud cry, as in fright or extreme pain; to shriek; to screech.
examples: The man screamed in agony and collapsed.
Scream out in/with something People ran for the exits, screaming out in terror.

definition: A physical divider intended to block an area from view, or provide shelter from something dangerous.
examples: Move your cursor to the top of the screen.
An LCD/plasma screen

definition: To filter by passing through a screen.
examples: The programme was screened on 24 December.
The fight was screened live all over the world.

definition: Mesh material that is used to screen (as in a "screen door").
examples: This will be the movie's first screening in this country.

definition: A device that has a helical function.
examples: Now tighten all the screws.
One of the screws is loose.

definition: To connect or assemble pieces using a screw.
examples: Now screw down the lid.
The bookcase is screwed to the wall.

definition: A writing; a written document.
examples: That line isn't in the original script.
To write/read a script

definition: Intense study of someone or something.
examples: The documents should be available for public scrutiny.
Her argument doesn't really stand up to scrutiny.

definition: A three dimensional work of art created by shaping malleable objects and letting them harden or by chipping away pieces from a rock (sculpting).
examples: A sculpture garden/park
He collects modern sculpture.

definition: A large body of salt water.
examples: He was shot down into the sea off (= near) Japan.
By the sea a cottage by the sea

definition: A pinniped (Pinnipedia), particularly an earless seal (true seal) or eared seal.
examples: The letter bore the president's seal.

definition: To hunt seals.
examples: A sealed bid (= one that is kept in a sealed envelope and therefore remains secret until all other bids have been received)
Make sure you've signed the cheque before sealing the envelope.

definition: An attempt to find something.
examples: Police conducted a fingertip search of the garden.
The search is on (= has begun) for someone to fill the post.

definition: To look in (a place) for something.
examples: Police searched for clues in the area.
+ adv./prep. The customs officers searched through our bags.

definition: Each of the four divisions of a year: spring, summer, autumn (fall) and winter.
examples: The changing seasons
Autumn is my favourite season.

definition: Something to be sat upon.
examples: A child seat (= for a child in a car)
A window/an aisle seat (= on a plane or train)

definition: To put an object into a place where it will rest; to fix; to set firm.
examples: Please wait to be seated (= in a restaurant, etc.).
She was wondering where to seat her guests.

definition: (with superlative) After the first; at the second rank.
examples: The women's team came in fourth and the men finished second.
We're not here to run second. We want to win races.

definition: Something that is number two in a series.
examples: The second of June/June 2nd
This is the second time it's happened.

definition: Something that is number two in a series.
examples: Every… seconds The light flashes every five seconds.
For… seconds For several seconds he did not reply.

definition: Next in order to the first or primary; of second place in origin, rank, etc.
examples: The secondary curriculum

definition: In the second place.
examples: Firstly, it's expensive, and secondly, it's too slow.
Secondly, and importantly, cultural influences on behaviour are discussed.

definition: Being or kept hidden.
examples: Secret information/meetings/talks
A secret passage leading to the beach

definition: A piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden.
examples: He made no secret of his ambition (= he didn't try to hide it).
It's no secret that the past few years have been challenging for the industry.

definition: Someone entrusted with a secret; a confidant.
examples: Secretary to somebody/something He is secretary to the board of governors.
Please contact my secretary to make an appointment.

definition: A cutting; a part cut out from the rest of something.
examples: The tail section of the plane
Section of something That section of the road is still closed.

definition: Section.
examples: She works in the voluntary sector (= organizations that do not make a profit).
We have seen rapid growth in the services sector.

definition: Not specifically religious; lay or civil, as opposed to clerical.
examples: We live in a largely secular society.

definition: Free from attack or danger; protected.
examples: It's not a very secure way to make a living.
The future of the company looks secure.

definition: To make safe; to relieve from apprehensions of, or exposure to, danger; to guard; to protect.
examples: The delegation has secured the promise of a ceasefire.
She secured 2 000 votes.

definition: The condition of not being threatened, especially physically, psychologically, emotionally, or financially.
examples: The two countries agreed to work together to strengthen border security.
Passwords are a very important security measure.

definition: (stative) To perceive or detect with the eyes, or as if by sight.
examples: He recalls seeing his father sitting at the kitchen table.
See somebody/something doing something She was seen running away from the scene of the crime.

definition: A fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant.
examples: A packet of wild flower seeds
Seed potatoes (= used for planting)

definition: To try to find; to look for; to search for.
examples: Police are not seeking anyone else in connection with the deaths.
Seek for something/somebody (British English) They sought in vain for somewhere to shelter.

definition: One who seeks.
examples: The new attraction is expected to draw pleasure seekers from across the region.
Seekers after the truth

definition: To appear; to look outwardly; to be perceived as.
examples: It seems to somebody (that)… It seems to me that teachers have to work pretty hard.
Seem as though… It always seemed as though they would get married.

definition: As it appears; apparently.
examples: It was a seemingly impossible task.
A seemingly endless journey

definition: A length of some object.
examples: Lines divided the area into segments.
The changes will affect only a small segment of the population.

definition: To deliberately take hold of; to grab or capture.
examples: Seize something from somebody She tried to seize the gun from him.
She seized hold of my hand.

definition: Infrequently, rarely.
examples: He had seldom seen a child with so much talent.
They seldom watch television these days.

definition: To choose one or more elements of a set, especially a set of options.
examples: Select somebody/something to do something Six theatre companies have been selected to take part in this year's festival.
Select somebody/something a randomly selected sample of 23 schools

definition: A process by which heritable traits conferring survival and reproductive advantage to individuals, or related individuals, tend to be passed on to succeeding generations and become more frequent in a population, whereas other less favourable traits tend to become eliminated; the differential survival and reproduction of phenotypes.
examples: His unexpected selection as party leader
Jury selection in the cases is due to begin next week.

definition: Of or relating to the process of selection.
examples: The selective breeding of cattle
The socially selective nature of population changes

definition: One individual's personality, character, demeanor, or disposition.
examples: You'll soon be feeling your old self again (= feeling well or happy again).
Only with a few people could she be her real self (= show what she was really like rather than what she pretended to be).

definition: (ditransitive) To transfer goods or provide services in exchange for money.
examples: His father went bankrupt and the family had to sell their home.
The shares were sold in the open market.

definition: A class held for advanced studies in which students meet regularly to discuss original research, under the guidance of a professor.
examples: Teaching is by lectures and seminars.

definition: A member, normally elected, in the house or chamber of a legislature called a senate. The legislatures of the United States and Canada have senators.
examples: She has served as a Democratic senator for North Carolina since 2009.

definition: To make something (such as an object or message) go from one place to another.
examples: A radio signal was sent to the spacecraft.
Can you send me a link to the website?

definition: Older; superior.
examples: A senior partner in a law firm
The meeting should be chaired by the most senior person present.

definition: A physical feeling or perception from something that comes into contact with the body; something sensed.
examples: I had a sensation of falling, as if in a dream.
A tingling/burning sensation

definition: Any of the manners by which living beings perceive the physical world: for humans sight, smell, hearing, touch, taste.
examples: One of the most important things in a partner is a sense of humour (= the ability to find things funny or make people laugh).
Alex doesn't have any dress sense (= does not know which clothes look attractive).

definition: To use biological senses: to either see, hear, smell, taste, or feel.
examples: Sense somebody/something doing something He sensed someone moving around behind him.
Thomas, she sensed, could convince anyone of anything.

definition: Perceptible by the senses.
examples: I think the sensible thing would be to take a taxi home.

definition: Having the faculty of sensation; pertaining to the senses.
examples: Schools must be sensitive to the needs of students from different backgrounds.
A sensitive and caring man

definition: The quality or state of being sensitive; sensitiveness.
examples: Sensitivity to the needs of children
She pointed out with tact and sensitivity exactly where he had gone wrong.

definition: The decision or judgement of a jury or court; a verdict.
examples: I was too stunned to finish my sentence.
Let's take that paragraph apart sentence by sentence.

definition: To declare a sentence on a convicted person; to doom; to condemn to punishment.
examples: Sentence somebody to do something The judge sentenced him to hang.
Sentence somebody to something for something A court sentenced them to nine-year jail terms for fraud and tax evasion.

definition: A general thought, feeling, or sense.
examples: Public sentiment is against any change to the law.
The spread of nationalist sentiments

definition: Apart from (the rest); not connected to or attached to (anything else).
examples: Write a list of names on a separate piece of paper.
They have begun to sleep in separate rooms.

definition: To divide (a thing) into separate parts.
examples: Separate something Separate the eggs (= separate the yolk from the white).
Stir the sauce constantly so that it does not separate.

definition: The act of disuniting two or more things, or the condition of being separated.
examples: Separation between A and B the need for a clear separation between Church and State
Separation from somebody/something the state’s eventual separation from the federation

definition: The ninth month of the year, between August and October.
examples: We went to Japan last September.
(North American English) The meeting is on September fifth.

definition: A set of things next to each other in a set order; a series.

definition: Having to do with or arranged in a series.

definition: A number of things that follow on one after the other or are connected one after the other.
examples: She has a small part in a drama series for radio.
Her stories have been made into a TV series.

definition: Without humor or expression of happiness; grave in manner or disposition.

definition: (manner) In a serious or literal manner.

Migraines can seriously affect your quality of life.

definition: One who is hired to perform regular household or other duties, and receives compensation. As opposed to a slave.
examples: A faithful/devoted/trusted servant
Servant of somebody one of the servants of the king of Persia

definition: (personal) To provide a service (or, by extension, a product, especially food or drink).
examples: Serve something to somebody They served a wonderful meal to more than fifty delegates.

definition: An act of being of assistance to someone.
examples: The charity provides a vital service to the local community.
The government aims to improve public services, especially education.

definition: An informal gathering of musicians to play music, especially improvised jazz or a similar genre.
examples: A morning/afternoon session
The club held football coaching sessions for children in the area.

definition: A punch for setting nails in wood.
examples: This is an unusual set of circumstances.
A set of false teeth

definition: To put (something) down, to rest.

definition: Equipment designed for a particular purpose; an apparatus.

What’s the set-up in your family—who does the cooking?

definition: The time, place and circumstance in which something (such as a story or picture) is set; context; scenario.

A rural/an ideal/a beautiful/an idyllic setting

definition: To conclude or resolve (something):.

definition: The act of settling.

definition: Someone who settles in a new location, especially one who takes up residence in a previously uninhabited place; a colonist.

definition: An area of land in private ownership (as opposed to common land).

definition: Very bad or intense.
examples: Severe weather/storms

definition: In a severe manner.

definition: Arising from the fact of being male or female; pertaining to sex or gender, or to the social relations between the sexes.
examples: He has not threatened them, or made overtly sexual remarks.

definition: The quality of being sexual; that which is characterized or distinguished by sex.
examples: The psychology of human sexuality
Her overt sexuality shocked cinema audiences.

definition: (of a person) Having sex appeal; suggestive of sex.
examples: The sexy lead singer
She looked incredibly sexy in a black evening gown.

definition: Darkness where light, particularly sunlight, is blocked.
examples: In the shade The temperature can reach 40°C in the shade.
The trees provide shade for the animals in the summer.

definition: A dark image projected onto a surface where light (or other radiation) is blocked by the shade of an object.
examples: (figurative) He didn't want to cast a shadow on (= spoil) their happiness.
The shadows lengthened as the sun went down.

definition: The act of shaking or being shaken; tremulous or back-and-forth motion.
examples: Give the bottle a good shake before opening.
She gave him a shake to wake him.

definition: To cause (something) to move rapidly in opposite directions alternatingly.
examples: The whole house shakes when a train goes past.
Shake somebody/something Shake the bottle well before use.

definition: Having little depth; significantly less deep than wide.
examples: Shallow roots (= that grow near the surface of the ground)
They were playing in the shallow end (= of the swimming pool).

definition: Uncomfortable or painful feeling due to recognition or consciousness of one's own impropriety or dishonor or something being exposed that should have been kept private.
examples: What a shame they couldn't come.
What happened was a real shame.

definition: The status or condition of something.
examples: In shape The island was originally circular in shape.

definition: To create or make.
examples: Shape something This tool is used for shaping wood.
Tools for cutting and shaping metal

definition: Having been given a shape, especially a curved shape.
examples: A huge balloon shaped like a giant cow

definition: A portion of something, especially a portion given or allotted to someone.

definition: To give part of what one has to somebody else to use or consume.
examples: Parents said there was insufficient room for the two schools to share space.

examples: The major shareholders in the company

definition: A woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis.

examples: On a shelf The book I wanted was on the top shelf.

definition: A hard external covering of an animal.

definition: A refuge, haven or other cover or protection from something.

definition: To provide cover from damage or harassment; to shield; to protect.

definition: A modifier key whose main function is shifting between two or more functions of any of certain other keys (usually by pressing Shift and the other button simultaneously).
examples: I've just finished an eight-hour shift.
On a shift to be on the day/night shift at the factory

definition: (sometimes figurative) To move from one place to another; to redistribute.
examples: Shift from somebody/something to somebody/something The action of the novel shifts from Paris to London.

definition: To emit light.

Shine with something (figurative) Her eyes were shining with excitement.

definition: Reflecting light.
examples: A shiny object/surface

definition: A water-borne vessel generally larger than a boat.
examples: A ship’s company (= the crew of a ship)

definition: To send by water-borne transport.
examples: Within four years they were shipping fabrics to customers in Australia.
The company ships its goods all over the world.

definition: The transportation of goods.
examples: The canal is open to shipping.
International shipping lanes (= routes for ships)

definition: An article of clothing that is worn on the upper part of the body, and often has sleeves, either long or short, that cover the arms.
examples: In a shirt A man in a striped shirt sat alone in the corner.
She took a pen from her shirt pocket.

definition: A sudden, heavy impact.
examples: Her shock at finding Elizabeth there was obvious.
Shock of something The party has hardly recovered from the shock of its defeat in May.

Shock somebody President Kennedy's assassination in Dallas on November 22, 1963, shocked the world.

definition: Surprised, startled, confused, or taken aback.

Shocked that… Neighbours were shocked that such an attack could happen in their area.

definition: Inspiring shock; startling.
examples: A shocking waste of money
It is shocking that they involved children in the crime.

definition: A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer upper part made of leather or synthetic material. Shoes generally do not extend above the ankle, as opposed to boots, which do.
examples: He ran out into the street despite having no shoes on.
The sole of the shoe is made of hard leather.

definition: To launch a projectile.
examples: Don't shoot—I surrender.
Shoot something from something He shot an arrow from his bow.

definition: An instance of shooting with a gun or other weapon.
examples: Police rushed to the scene of the shooting and found one person dead and three wounded.
There was no direct link between the two fatal shootings.

definition: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public; originally only a physical location, but now a virtual establishment as well.
examples: Shop owners in the area

definition: To visit stores or shops to browse or explore merchandise, especially with the intention of buying such merchandise.
examples: Shop for something to shop for food
They shop in the same supermarket.

definition: The process of buying goods or services, or searching for those suitable to buy.
examples: She is in the fashionable shopping area of London.
They go on endless shopping trips.

definition: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
examples: To swim from the boat to the shore

definition: Having a small distance from one end or edge to another, either horizontally or vertically.
examples: She decided to cut her hair short.
He had short curly hair.

definition: Of or pertaining to the near or immediate future.

His short-term memory (= the ability to remember things that happened a short time ago) is failing.

definition: A lack or deficiency; an insufficient amount.
examples: There is no shortage of (= there are plenty of) things to do in the town.
Food/housing/water shortages

definition: In a short or brief time or manner; quickly.
examples: She arrived shortly after us.

definition: The result of launching a projectile or bullet.
examples: Shot to something She was killed by a single shot to the head.
The man fired several shots from his pistol.

definition: The part of an animal's body between the base of the neck and forearm socket.
examples: Your left/right shoulder
She shrugged her shoulders (= showing that she didn't know or care).

definition: A loud burst of voice or voices; a violent and sudden outcry, especially that of a multitude expressing joy, triumph, exultation, anger, or animated courage.
